title: The Causes of World War I
summary: The long-term causes of World War I (militarism, alliances, imperialism and nationalism), the assassination at Sarajevo, and how a local crisis became a world war.

notes.text: **World War I** (the First World War or 'Great War') lasted from **1914 to 1918**. It was fought mainly in Europe but involved countries and colonies from around the world. More than 16 million people died. Historians remember the long-term causes with the word **MAIN**.

notes.caption: The MAIN causes
rows: **M**ilitarism
Building up large armies and navies and believing war is a good way to solve problems
The naval arms race between Britain and Germany to build Dreadnought battleships
**A**lliances
Agreements to help each other in war
Triple Alliance and Triple Entente divided Europe into two armed camps
**I**mperialism
Competition for colonies and empire
Germany wanted 'a place in the sun'; crises over Morocco in 1905 and 1911
**N**ationalism
Strong pride in one's nation, sometimes the belief that it is better than others; also the desire of peoples to have their own country
Serbian nationalists wanted to free Slavs ruled by Austria-Hungary

notes.problem: Match each to militarism, alliances, imperialism or nationalism: (a) Britain and Germany racing to build warships, (b) European powers competing for African colonies, (c) Serbs wanting a united South Slav state.
steps: (c) A people wanting their own nation is **nationalism**.

notes.caption: The two armed camps of 1914. A single shooting in Sarajevo pulled both alliances into war.

notes.text: **Archduke Franz Ferdinand**, heir to the throne of Austria-Hungary, and his wife Sophie were visiting **Sarajevo** in Bosnia, which Austria-Hungary had taken over. They were shot dead by **Gavrilo Princip**, a 19-year-old Bosnian Serb who belonged to a nationalist group called the **Black Hand**.

items: Austria-Hungary blamed Serbia and, with Germany's support (the 'blank cheque'), sent Serbia a harsh ultimatum.
**28 July**: Austria-Hungary declared war on Serbia.
Russia, protector of the Slavs, mobilised its army to support Serbia.
**1 August**: Germany declared war on Russia, and on **3 August** on France, Russia's ally.
Germany's **Schlieffen Plan** meant attacking France quickly through neutral **Belgium**.
**4 August**: Britain declared war on Germany to defend Belgian neutrality (the 1839 Treaty of London) and support France.

notes.caption: How one assassination became a world war in about five weeks.

notes.label: Key idea
notes.text: The assassination was the **immediate cause** (the trigger). The alliance system turned a local conflict in the Balkans into a war between all the great powers within about a week.

notes.title: Source D: The 'blank cheque' (a paraphrase of Germany's assurance to Austria-Hungary, July 1914)
notes.text: Austria-Hungary must deal with Serbia firmly, and Germany will stand by her side as a faithful ally, whatever the consequences.

Because the European powers had empires, the war quickly became a **world war**: soldiers and labourers from India, Africa, Australia, Canada and New Zealand fought for Britain and France, and fighting took place in African colonies as well.

notes.title: How one murder became a world war
notes.problem: Explain the chain of events after the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand on 28 June 1914.
steps: Austria-Hungary blamed Serbia and declared war on 28 July.
Germany, Austria-Hungary's ally, declared war on Russia and then France.
Germany invaded Belgium to reach France, and Britain declared war on 4 August.
notes.answer: The alliance system turned a regional crisis into a European war within weeks.
